title: Reserve Workbench: Compact KPI strip and elasticity controls prototype
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a low-height 'Reserve Workbench' control strip for Dedicated capacity that surfaces essential GPU pool KPIs and lets operators make rapid elasticity decisions without leaving a single compact panel. The goal is a single-row control that fits in the fleet view and pool detail header: - Left: compact KPI chips (utilization, active sessions, p50/p95 latency, queue depth, GPU memory headroom) - Center: cost-elasticity visualization (small sparkline + 3-point projection with 'current', 'after-change', '30m forecast') - Right: lightweight controls (min/max nodes slider, burst budget dial, safety SLO toggle and preview, 'simulate cost' CTA)
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prototype screens exist for 3 breakpoints (desktop wide, narrow, and condensed row). 2) KPI chips map to telemetry signals and have hover tooltips with 2-line explanations and one-link to logs/dashboard. 3) Elasticity slider enforces min <= current <= max and shows estimated cost delta before submission. 4) Burst dial accepts GPU-hours or tokens/min input, with clear conversion help text. 5) Simulate flow runs a client-side cost estimation and shows 3 scenarios. 6) Accessibility: controls reachable by keyboard, contrast meets AA, aria labels present. 7) Handoff-ready spec with token count math and event names for telemetry.
design_notes: - Avoid large modal flows - inline 'preview' panel should appear below strip. - Use a condensed visual language: micro sparklines, colored badges, and a single action button group. - Cost projection uses a clipped area chart with projected error band to avoid false precision. - Safety SLO toggle will attach an automated guardrail (auto-throttle to scale-down-prevent) — figma prototype demonstrates behavior. - Consider adding an 'ops quick revert' control that records last 3 changes and allows 1-click rollback.
engineering_notes: - Telemetry mapping: util -> metric.heap_gpu_util_pct, p95 -> api.inference_latency_p95_ms, queue -> pool.request_queue_len. - Proposed telemetry events: reserve_workbench.simulate, reserve_workbench.commit, reserve_workbench.rollback. - Backend needs new endpoint /pools/:id/preview-elasticity that returns estimated token costs and latency impact (mocked for prototype). - PR for UI skeleton: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/9876 (WIP).
review_feedback: PM (Jules Ramirez): Love the compact approach; request that the 'simulate' must include cost-per-hour and cost-per-1M-tokens estimates.
Eng (Lena Ortiz): Concerned about real-time telemetry cost; recommend simulated preview be client-side with server-side verification on commit. Added dependency ENG-4512.
Design (Ravi Nair): Suggest replacing numeric-only burst dial with a dual-mode input (slider + precise numeric field) for fast and exact edits.
Accessibility (Aisha Khan): Keyboard order should be KPI chips -> elasticity slider -> burst dial -> simulate -> commit. Need aria-describedby on the projection chart.
UX Research (Samira Lopez): Prototype usability test (5 operators) showed reduce mistakes when confirmation CTA shows estimated cost delta in red/green.
decisions_made: Keep control strip single-row for visibility in fleet list and pool details.
Client-side simulation for instant feedback; server-side verification required on 'commit'.
Expose both GPU-hours and token throughput for burst input; default unit derived from pool preference.
Add a 1-click rollback stored in audit logs for operational safety.
open_questions: How should projected latency impact be computed for heterogeneous workloads? (Eng to propose model by 2025-01-24)
Should the burst budget be billed immediately at commit or amortized across projected duration? (Finance input needed)
Do we also expose per-route cost signals in the compact strip or keep route-level cost in the detailed panel?
usability_test_plan: Recruit 5 platform operators (internal) for 30-minute remote sessions: tasks include set min/max nodes, configure a 2-hour burst, run simulate, commit, and revert. Measure task time, errors, and perceived confidence. Capture screen recordings and SUS score.
qa_checklist: Cost projection math matches server stub response
Simulate does not mutate server state
Rollback restores previous numeric config and logs an audit event
Visual regression tests for compact strip at 3 breakpoints
